answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network enforces cryptographic stake burning where registering each node costs S(k)=C*k^2 burned tokens. By tagging identity shards with hash roots like umber, lotus, and walnut, verification requires burning non-refundable stake across all three tiers. This imposes superlinear cost scaling on attackers, making mass spoofing exponentially ruinous while authentic economic agents remain sustainable.
